description_html:
• (01:10) - High Interest Rate Phenomenon
  • (17:46) - WSJ Opinion: 'The People Get a Vote on AI Safety'
  • (30:00) - Timeline Reactions
  • (51:45) - Driscoll's China Bet Backfires
  • (57:47) - Jim VandeHei, co-founder and CEO of Axios, discusses his book *Simplify*, which presents a system for increasing productivity by focusing on high-value work and eliminating or automating unnecessary tasks. He also explores AI’s potential to streamline business operations, expand media distribution, augment employees, and create new opportunities without replacing essential human creativity, leadership, and judgment.
  • (01:15:00) - Steve Menneto, president and CEO of Malibu Boats, discusses the company’s nine-brand portfolio, global expansion, vertical integration, and nearly $1 billion in revenue. He also covers boating-market trends, premium consumer demand, electric and autonomous technologies, skilled-labor needs, defense opportunities, and the customer purchasing journey.
  • (01:30:00) - Matthew Wilson discusses Jack and Jill, an AI-assisted hiring platform where he serves as co-founder and CEO. He explains how its agents connect professionals with suitable jobs and companies with qualified candidates, reducing the noise created by AI-generated applications and recruitment outreach, and notes that the company has raised $40 million.
  • (01:39:25) - Rune Kvist, an entrepreneur focused on frontier AI risk, discusses his company’s $40 million Series A and its work developing AI safety standards, audits, and insurance. He explains how liability frameworks and insurer-led oversight could align incentives, improve trust, and enable continued AI innovation while managing catastrophic risks.
  • (01:48:59) - Tyler Bahl, a marketing executive at Activision, discusses his career journey and work bringing Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 to market. He explains the franchise’s marketing strategy, gameplay evolution, creator partnerships, AI use, esports, and efforts to serve its broad community.
  • (02:23:03) - Stephen Colbert and Josh Kline discuss his passion for "The Lord of the Rings" and their work developing Scripto, a collaborative production platform designed to improve communication and efficiency across entertainment teams. The comedian, writer, and television host also reflects on sustainable creative processes, expresses optimism about filmmaking, and encourages aspiring creators to stop waiting for permission and make their own work.
  • (02:44:58) - James Cadwallader discusses Profound’s $180 million funding round and its rapid adoption among major global brands. He explains how Profound helps marketers understand and improve their visibility across AI platforms, create content for AI agents, and manage advertising, with the broader goal of becoming the leading AI marketing company.
